title: Shoreline Guard
intro: Water carries soil down a slope the way waves and rain wear down a Michigan shoreline. Test two barriers against no barrier.
note: This is a model that uses the lesson's backup numbers, one trial each. Your own water-tray trials in the lesson still count, and repeating them makes the evidence stronger.
summary: A fair test changes only the barrier and uses the same slope and the same water. Grass let 5 spoons of sediment move and the wall 7, against 12 with no barrier, so both helped and grass helped more. One trial each is a start; repeating the test makes the claim stronger.

rounds.question: Water runs down a soil slope and carries sediment away. Which barrier reduces erosion more?

factors.label: Amount of water poured
factors.held: The same amount of water each time
factors.why: If some tests get more water, the water could cause the difference, not the barrier.

factors.label: Steepness of the slope
factors.held: The same slope and the same amount of soil
factors.why: If the slope changes, the slope could cause the difference, not the barrier.

factors.label: How you pour
factors.held: The same pour, from the same spot
factors.why: If the pouring changes, the pouring could cause the difference, not the barrier.

rounds.measure: Sediment that moved, in spoonfuls (fewer means the barrier helped)

reads.q: Which test let the least sediment move?

choices.label: Wall
choices.why: The wall let 7 spoons move. Another test let fewer move.

choices.label: Grass
choices.why: Grass let 5 spoons move, the fewest. No barrier let 12 move.

choices.label: No barrier
choices.why: No barrier let the most sediment move, 12 spoons.

reads.q: Each barrier was tested once. What would make the evidence stronger?

choices.label: Pour more water on the grass only
choices.why: That would make the test unfair. The water must stay the same for every barrier.

choices.label: Repeat each test and compare the results
choices.why: Yes. One trial can be a messy one. Repeats show whether the pattern holds.

choices.label: Stop, because one test is always enough
choices.why: One trial can be a fluke. Think about how to check it.

choices.label: grass reduces more harm than the wall.
choices.why: Yes. Both helped, and grass let less sediment move.

choices.label: the wall reduces more harm than grass.
choices.why: The wall let 7 spoons move and grass let 5. Check which number is smaller.

choices.label: barriers do not help.
choices.why: Both barriers let less sediment move than no barrier.

choices.label: erosion of the slope by moving water.
choices.why: Yes. Moving water carries soil away.

choices.label: the Sun drying the soil.
choices.why: The Sun is not part of this test. Think about what carries the soil down the slope.

choices.label: 5 spoons moved with grass, 7 with the wall and 12 with no barrier.
choices.why: Yes. That matches the three results.

choices.label: 12 spoons moved with grass.
choices.why: Twelve spoons moved with no barrier.
